variables.reason: The ledger defines Ra as "the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations" which is the arithmetic mean (mean absolute deviation) of surface height about its mean. The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness gives the canonical definition as "arithmetic mean roughness" (symbols Ra; R_a) with si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, directly matching the physical meaning and units of Ra in the problem statement. That KB entry therefore supports the candidate exponent L=1 (length) and the zeros for other base dimensions because it documents that Ra is a dimensional roughness-height statistic with units of length.

The ledger defines kt as the "peak-to-valley height", an amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height explicitly lists this quantity (symbols include kt) with si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, confirming it is a length. Therefore the candidate exponents with L=1 and all other base exponents zero are correct for kt in the original problem context.

The ledger defines k_rms as the "root-mean-square height" (RMS roughness), i.e. the root-mean-square fluctuation of surface height about its mean. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height gives this canonical definition and records si_dimension: L and si_unit: m, confirming k_rms is a dimensional length measure. The candidate vector L=1 (length) with other exponents zero matches this KB entry and the physical meaning in the problem.

The ledger defines Sk as "the third central moment of roughness height fluctuations divided by the cube of their root-mean-square height", i.e. the standardized third moment (skewness) of the surface-height distribution. The KB record pq_height_skewness gives this canonical definition and records si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That supports the candidate exponents all zero (dimensionless) for Sk and aligns with its role as a shape/statistical parameter of the height distribution in the original problem.

The ledger defines Ku as "the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations", i.e. the standardized fourth moment of the surface-height distribution. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis lists this quantity with si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). Thus the candidate's all-zero exponent vector (dimensionless) for Ku is correct and directly supported by the KB record for the variable as used in the problem.

The ledger defines ES as the "effective streamwise slope of the roughness" (mean absolute gradient of surface height in a specified horizontal direction). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope gives this canonical definition and explicitly states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and is therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This directly supports the candidate exponents with all zeros for ES.

The ledger defines Po as "surface porosity", a fraction of void or open area and therefore a dimensionless quantity. The KB record pq_porosity lists porosity with si_dimension: 1 and notes it is a dimensionless fraction. The candidate's all-zero exponent vector for Po is therefore correct and supported by the KB entry.
